identification.full_name: Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM (IMERG) Late Run
identification.product: GPM IMERG Late Precipitation L3 Half Hourly
identification.project: Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), NASA and JAXA
identification.doi_note: DOI for the half-hourly Late Run product, not the Early or Final Run
identification.description: A NASA Level-3 global precipitation dataset from the GPM mission, combining observations from many satellite instruments into gridded estimates. The Late Run is made for near-real-time use, with about 12–14 hours of latency.

archives.name: NASA GES DISC
archives.description: Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center; primary public archive and distribution service

archives.name: NASA PPS
archives.description: Precipitation Processing System; operational processing and distribution archive for GPM products

archives.name: NASA Earthdata
archives.description: Discovery and access infrastructure for NASA Earth science datasets

archives.name: AWS Open Data Registry
archives.description: Cloud-hosted access to the GES DISC IMERG dataset

access_endpoints.name: IMERG Late Run – daily data (GES DISC)
IMERG Late Run – AWS Open Data Registry

access_note: Use GES DISC to download half-hourly or daily data, subset areas and read metadata. PPS is useful for operational products and may need registration.

curator.name: NASA Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC)
curator.role: Dataset archive, curation and distribution; support through NASA Earthdata Support

leads.name: George J. Huffman
leads.role: GPM Project Scientist; lead of the GPM Multi-satellite Algorithm Team; scientific lead for IMERG

people.note: George Huffman is the scientific lead; GES DISC manages the archived dataset and its distribution.

instruments.summary: Passive microwave radiometers and sounders on the GPM constellation, plus geostationary infrared sensors

categories.name: Infrared (IR) sensors
categories.role: Cloud-top information used to fill gaps between microwave overpasses

platforms.instrument: SAPHIR – Sounder for Atmospheric Profiling of Humidity in the Intertropics by Radiometry

instruments.gauge_adjustment: Climatological (the Final Run uses monthly gauge analyses instead)
instruments.note: A merged satellite product, not a single instrument. Microwave observations give the main estimates; infrared fills time gaps through interpolation.

temporal.start_note: Confirmed on the NASA GPM IMERG page (gpm.nasa.gov/taxonomy/term/1415); covers the TRMM era (1998–2015) and GPM era (2014–present) through reprocessing.

other_frequencies.availability: By aggregation; not a standard Late Run product

spatial.note: Near-global, with limits in a few grid boxes very close to the poles. Useful over oceans and remote areas without gauges.

data_format.format: HDF5 (.H5); NetCDF (.nc4); GeoTIFF (.tif); PNG images (.png); OPeNDAP online access

formats.description: Online access: read data remotely without downloading whole files

data_format.note: The formats offered depend on the download source and product.

status.label: Ongoing (near real time)
evidence: NASA continues to produce near-real-time estimates
New observations are added about every 30 minutes
The algorithm has had version updates; V07B is the latest processing generation
Historical data were reprocessed back to January 1998

related_products.name: IMERG Final Run
related_products.difference: Uses monthly gauge analyses; not the same product as the Late Run
